Find the area bounded by the polar curve $r={e}^{3\theta }$ for $0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,$ as shown above.
after.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

When $r(\theta )={e}^{3\theta }$, ${\theta }_{1}=0$ and ${\theta }_{2}=2\pi $, this gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{({e}^{3\theta })}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{e}^{6\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{6}{e}^{6\theta }{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{12}({e}^{12\pi }-{e}^{0}) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}({e}^{12\pi }-1).\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14066449/assets/c06da8f06e8d640c23dbd81885fdd1bd5e5d89b15b1729cacd82ac52f301e44d.png)

Find the area bounded by the polar curve $r={e}^{3\theta }$ for $0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,$ as shown above.
content.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

When $r(\theta )={e}^{3\theta }$, ${\theta }_{1}=0$ and ${\theta }_{2}=2\pi $, this gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{({e}^{3\theta })}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{e}^{6\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{6}{e}^{6\theta }{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{12}({e}^{12\pi }-{e}^{0}) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}({e}^{12\pi }-1).\end{aligned}
$$
